title: Wheelchair Basketball: training overview
d: Wheelchair Basketball training builds the fitness, skills, and tactics the rules demand.
definition: Wheelchair Basketball training builds the fitness, skills, and tactics the rules demand.
description: Wheelchair Basketball training has three pillars: the physical engine, the technical skills, and the tactical brain. The rules define the demands — 5 per side over four 10-minute quarters — and training reverses them into a program: energy systems for the duration, strength for the collisions and jumps, skills for the techniques, tactics for the decisions. This database covers all four across a season, from first preseason week to championship taper.

title: Strength program
d: Wheelchair Basketball strength work: Jump training plus shoulder care: Olympic lifts for power, rotator-cuff work for the hitting shoulder..
definition: Wheelchair Basketball strength work: Jump training plus shoulder care: Olympic lifts for power, rotator-cuff work for the hitting shoulder..
description: Strength training for Wheelchair Basketball: Jump training plus shoulder care: Olympic lifts for power, rotator-cuff work for the hitting shoulder. Train strength twice a week in season, three times out of it. Lift for the sport, not for the mirror — every exercise should answer which on-field action it improves. Keep a training log; progressive overload over months is what separates good from great.

title: Conditioning plan
d: Wheelchair Basketball conditioning mirrors four 10-minute quarters: work-to-rest matched to the game clock.
definition: Wheelchair Basketball conditioning mirrors four 10-minute quarters: work-to-rest matched to the game clock.
description: Conditioning for Wheelchair Basketball must mirror the game clock: four 10-minute quarters. Build the aerobic base first — it speeds recovery between hard efforts — then layer sport-specific intervals. Never sacrifice skill sessions for extra running; tired athletes learn bad technique. Monitor with resting heart rate and repeat-sprint tests.

title: Skill acquisition
d: Learn Wheelchair Basketball skills in three stages: grooved, pressured, then match-random.
definition: Learn Wheelchair Basketball skills in three stages: grooved, pressured, then match-random.
description: Skill learning in Wheelchair Basketball follows blocked-to-random progression: first groove the movement alone, then add pressure, then randomize like a match. Ten thousand mindless reps engrave errors; one thousand deliberate reps with feedback engrave skill. Film everything — athletes cannot fix what they cannot see.

title: Tactical training
d: Wheelchair Basketball tactics are rehearsed, not improvised: walk, jog, full speed, then live.
definition: Wheelchair Basketball tactics are rehearsed, not improvised: walk, jog, full speed, then live.
description: Tactical training in Wheelchair Basketball: walk through the shape, jog it, run it full speed, then go live. Tactics fail when players think instead of recognize — so rehearse until recognition is instant. Review film weekly: pause at decisions and ask what the right choice was before revealing it.

title: Sports nutrition
d: Fuel Wheelchair Basketball: carbs for the work, protein for repair, timing around sessions.
definition: Fuel Wheelchair Basketball: carbs for the work, protein for repair, timing around sessions.
description: Nutrition for Wheelchair Basketball athletes: carbohydrate covers the training load, protein (about 1.6-2.2 g per kg daily) repairs it, and fluids with electrolytes cover the sweat. Eat a familiar meal 3 hours before competition and a carb-protein mix within 2 hours after. Supplements are the last one percent — food is the other ninety-nine.

title: Hydration plan
d: Wheelchair Basketball hydration: start hydrated, drink to thirst plus plan, replace after.
definition: Wheelchair Basketball hydration: start hydrated, drink to thirst plus plan, replace after.
description: Hydration for Wheelchair Basketball: weigh before and after sessions to learn your sweat rate, drink on a schedule in long events, and replace sodium in heat. Losing two percent of body mass to dehydration measurably impairs skill and decisions. Practice the race-day drinking plan in training — never try anything new on competition day.

title: Recovery methods
d: Recover from Wheelchair Basketball: sleep first, then easy movement, food, and stress control.
definition: Recover from Wheelchair Basketball: sleep first, then easy movement, food, and stress control.
description: Recovery from Wheelchair Basketball training ranks: sleep (8-9 hours for athletes) first, then light movement, then nutrition timing, then stress management. Ice baths and gadgets are minor compared to sleep. Track morning readiness — soreness, mood, resting heart rate — and adjust the day's load to it.

title: Sleep for athletes
d: Wheelchair Basketball athletes need 8-9 hours: sleep is when training adaptations happen.
definition: Wheelchair Basketball athletes need 8-9 hours: sleep is when training adaptations happen.
description: Sleep is the legal performance enhancer for Wheelchair Basketball: growth hormone peaks in deep sleep, skills consolidate overnight, and reaction time degrades measurably with debt. Keep the room cool, dark, and screen-free; keep wake time consistent even on weekends. Naps of 20-30 minutes help; long late naps hurt night sleep.

title: Mental skills
d: Train the Wheelchair Basketball mind: routines, self-talk, visualization, and pressure rehearsal.
definition: Train the Wheelchair Basketball mind: routines, self-talk, visualization, and pressure rehearsal.
description: Mental training for Wheelchair Basketball: a pre-performance routine that never changes, self-talk that is instructional not emotional, visualization of successful execution, and deliberate pressure practice. Confidence comes from preparation evidence — keep a log of good sessions to read before big events. Anxiety is normal; unmanaged anxiety is optional.

title: Season planning
d: Plan the Wheelchair Basketball year: base, build, peak, and transition phases.
definition: Plan the Wheelchair Basketball year: base, build, peak, and transition phases.
description: Season planning for Wheelchair Basketball runs in phases: base (volume and technique), build (intensity and tactics), peak (sharpen for championships), transition (rest and play). One peak per season for most athletes; trying to peak year-round peaks never. Schedule deload weeks every 3-4 weeks — adaptation happens in recovery.

title: Tapering
d: Taper for Wheelchair Basketball championships: cut volume 40-60%, keep intensity sharp.
definition: Taper for Wheelchair Basketball championships: cut volume 40-60%, keep intensity sharp.
description: The Wheelchair Basketball taper: 1-3 weeks out, cut training volume by 40 to 60 percent but keep some sharp intensity so the body stays awake. Sleep more, eat familiar food, trust the training. Most athletes taper too little and arrive flat, or train through and arrive tired — the taper is part of the program, not time off.

title: Youth development
d: Young Wheelchair Basketball athletes: sample many sports, prioritize fun and fundamentals.
definition: Young Wheelchair Basketball athletes: sample many sports, prioritize fun and fundamentals.
description: Youth Wheelchair Basketball development: before age 14, multi-sport sampling beats early specialization for both skill and health. Keep sessions short, playful, and technique-rich; measure success in smiles and improvement, not trophies. Never year-round single-sport training before puberty — overuse injuries end more careers than opponents do.

title: Injury prevention
d: Prevent Wheelchair Basketball injuries: warm up, strengthen the known weak links, manage load.
definition: Prevent Wheelchair Basketball injuries: warm up, strengthen the known weak links, manage load.
description: Injury prevention in Wheelchair Basketball targets the sport's known patterns: structured warm-ups (like FIFA 11+ style programs) cut injuries measurably, strength work protects joints, and load management — never spiking weekly volume more than about ten percent — prevents most overuse injuries. Report pain early; playing through sharp pain turns small problems into seasons lost.

title: Fitness testing
d: Test Wheelchair Basketball fitness: repeat the same battery every 6-8 weeks.
definition: Test Wheelchair Basketball fitness: repeat the same battery every 6-8 weeks.
description: Fitness testing for Wheelchair Basketball: pick 4-6 tests covering speed, endurance, power, and sport skill, and repeat the identical battery every 6-8 weeks. Tests direct the program — train the weakest result. Record everything; athletes who test improve faster because the numbers make progress visible.

title: Return to play
d: Return to Wheelchair Basketball after injury: criteria-based, not calendar-based.
definition: Return to Wheelchair Basketball after injury: criteria-based, not calendar-based.
description: Return to Wheelchair Basketball after injury follows criteria, not dates: full range of motion, strength symmetry, sport-specific movements pain-free, then controlled contact, then full training, then competition. Rushing back re-injures; the second injury is usually worse. Clearance from a clinician plus passing functional tests is the standard.

title: Pre-game routine
d: Wheelchair Basketball pre-game: same timeline, same warm-up, same mindset every time.
definition: Wheelchair Basketball pre-game: same timeline, same warm-up, same mindset every time.
description: The Wheelchair Basketball pre-game routine: fixed timeline from arrival, dynamic warm-up progressing to sport speed, equipment check, tactical reminders, then quiet focus. Routines calm nerves by making the unfamiliar familiar. Rehearse the routine before minor events so it is automatic for major ones.

title: Video analysis
d: Study Wheelchair Basketball film: your reps, opponents' tendencies, and elite models.
definition: Study Wheelchair Basketball film: your reps, opponents' tendencies, and elite models.
description: Video analysis in Wheelchair Basketball: review your own reps first (technique), then opponents (tendencies), then elite models (what great looks like). Keep clips short and specific — three clips with one fix each beats an hour of passive watching. Athletes who study film make better decisions under pressure.

title: Goal setting
d: Set Wheelchair Basketball goals in three layers: outcome, performance, and process.
definition: Set Wheelchair Basketball goals in three layers: outcome, performance, and process.
description: Goal setting for Wheelchair Basketball: outcome goals (win the league) motivate, performance goals (improve first-touch success) direct, and process goals (today's drill focus) control the day. Write them down, review weekly, and keep process goals in the majority — athletes control effort and execution, not scoreboards.

title: Cross-training
d: Cross-train for Wheelchair Basketball: swim, bike, or lift to build fitness without sport load.
definition: Cross-train for Wheelchair Basketball: swim, bike, or lift to build fitness without sport load.
description: Cross-training for Wheelchair Basketball keeps fitness growing while the sport-specific tissues rest: swimming for cardio without impact, cycling for legs without pounding, strength work for armor. One cross session weekly in season, more in the off-season. Variety also refreshes the mind — burnout ends more seasons than injuries do.

title: Equipment care
d: Wheelchair Basketball gear lasts longer and performs better with basic maintenance.
definition: Wheelchair Basketball gear lasts longer and performs better with basic maintenance.
description: Equipment care in Wheelchair Basketball: clean it, dry it, store it right, and inspect it before every session. Worn gear causes injuries — dead shoes, frayed ropes, cracked helmets retire on schedule, not after failure. Keep a spare of anything that would end your day if it broke.

title: Travel competition
d: Travel for Wheelchair Basketball events: control what you can — sleep, food, and warm-up.
definition: Travel for Wheelchair Basketball events: control what you can — sleep, food, and warm-up.
description: Travel competition in Wheelchair Basketball: arrive as early as the budget allows, bring familiar food, protect sleep across time zones, and scout the venue on arrival. Keep the pre-game routine identical to home — familiarity is calming. Pack backups of every critical item in carry-on.

title: Off-season
d: The Wheelchair Basketball off-season: rest first, then rebuild the base and fix weaknesses.
definition: The Wheelchair Basketball off-season: rest first, then rebuild the base and fix weaknesses.
description: The Wheelchair Basketball off-season has two halves: complete rest for 2-4 weeks (mental and physical), then base rebuilding with high volume and low pressure. Fix the weakest link identified in testing, try a new sport for athleticism, and return to preseason hungry. Athletes who skip the off-season borrow from next year.
